A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Middo framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning evaluations on two model families, baseline comparisons, component ablations, and dataset analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and reports revised benchmark values and an additional optimized-only training result.

M1.justification: The loss-based complexity selection, embedding-neighbor diversity augmentation, self-alignment quality refinement, and iterative training loop remain unchanged. Revised explanations and prompt spelling do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, Alpaca-4o-mini, and WizardLM, the same eight main evaluation benchmarks, and ARC-c in the appendix neighbor study. The additional subset condition does not introduce a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Alpaca-clean, both Superfiltering variants, Long, AlpaGasus, I-SHEEP, Alpaca-GPT4, and WizardLM. Middo Only becomes MiddOnly; no external comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported source of the retained 8.8k optimized-only row from Alpaca-4o-mini to Alpaca and adds a 24.9k Alpaca-4o-mini optimized-only condition. These are changes to documented comparison settings, without establishing reruns. Shared training and evaluation hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends the optimized-only control used to examine whether improvement depends on retaining more training data, now distinguishing both seed sources. Component ablations, neighbor/threshold/iteration sensitivity studies, and appendix case studies are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for performance. The standard deviations used in selection thresholds are unchanged and are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the Mistral/Wizard third-iteration scores, changing the average from 36.96 to 38.56 and the best iteration from two to three. Table 2 adds the 24.9k MiddOnly result averaging 42.77; its full-Alpaca row redisplays existing results. Figure 4 changes optimized maximum loss from 4.61 to 3.76, but omitted setting details prevent treating this as a demonstrated same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of loss selection, neighbor similarity, averaged quality scores, and the dynamic threshold remain equivalent. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same closed-loop data/model co-evolution contribution, three diagnostic signals, dataset-scale claim, and headline 7.15% accuracy-improvement claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now explicitly confines the example linking higher initial dataset quality to fewer optimal iterations to LLaMA-3.1-8B. The main mechanism interpretations and all four stated limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds code and data/model access links and identifies DataDreamer as the synthesis tool. Conversely, it removes explicit full-parameter/restarting-from-base wording and Figure 4's model/dataset/iteration specification. Table 4 also changes timing descriptions from less-than bounds to approximate values.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Gao's small-model coordination framework, Havrilla's synthetic-data survey, Shen's efficient-training survey, and DataDreamer. The selection-versus-synthesis positioning remains intact; publication and author updates to existing references do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: Local grammar edits, an expanded IFD explanation, MiddOnly terminology, revised affiliations, acknowledgments, and reordered appendix examples leave the main narrative structure intact. Citations switch to numbers, introducing mismatched MMLU/MATH references.

P2.justification: The two-column manuscript becomes a predominantly single-column report with branded, shaded front matter and running headers. Figures are resized and regrouped, loss/diversity plots are redrawn, Table 2 is expanded, the training-hyperparameter table is split, and appendix example figures are rearranged.

improvement.justification: The added access information and clearer separation of full-data and optimized-only conditions in Table 2 modestly improve reuse documentation and assessment of the data-size explanation. The model-specific qualification in Section 4.2 also improves precision. These gains are limited by shortened training and Figure 4 documentation and new citation mismatches; the revised scores do not themselves establish a stronger method.
